messages.author: aa37431deefd5020
messages.subject: Beginners Question
parts:
This is such a basic question that I am quite embarrassed to ask - but I
have searched the web, my ggplot book (Kindle version - not to be
recommended!) and Stackoverflow but cannot get an answer. I have a time
series from 1999-2011 monthly of temperature anomalies which range from
about -0.1 to +0.2. I want a plot of these which is much wider than it
is high. I can add an aspect ratio like:

p+opts(aspect.ratio = 0.5)

which works but leaves the title and X-axis label in the old position
(as noted at
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3936206/ggplot2-aspect-ratio-and-placing-title-axis-label-in-the-right-place).
I can do:

p+opts(aspect.ratio = 0.5)+ opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(colour =
'red', angle = 0, size = 10, vjust=15))

which moves the X-axis label upward. But I don't know what the units or
even direction of the 'vjust' parameter are. Can anyone explain?

Thanks,

Peter

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Beginners Question
parts:
Hi,

Can you not simply plot in a wide viewport?

print(qplot(1:10, 1:10), vp=viewport(width = 1, height = 0.5))

(untested)

HTH,

baptiste

messages.author: d674bddd91c6f700
messages.subject: Re: Beginners Question
parts:
This works ... but it sets the aspect ratio of the entire viewport,
not just of the plot itself. I read here:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3936206/ggplot2-aspect-ratio-and-placing-title-axis-label-in-the-right-place

that this behavior (the x-axis, y-axis labels not moving to follow the
modified aspect ratio) is a known limitation
in the current layout system. For kicks, I tried the development
version of ggplot2, but the behavior was the same.

- Dave

messages.subject: Re: Beginners Question

Yep, you are correct. It's a good thing that this thread is entitled
"Beginners Question", because I made a beginner's error and wasn't
actually using the develop branch (even though I thought I was). Once
I *really* made sure I was using the develop branch, you're right, the
axis labels move in concert with the change in the plot dimensions as
one changes the aspect ratio.

- Dave
